title: Refactor EKS control-plane Terraform module for Private control plane: upgrades, health checks, and drift remediation
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Context:
Redwood Private customers run a managed control plane in their VPC backed by EKS and supporting infra (AutoScalingGroups, private ALBs, security groups, KMS integration). The current Terraform module has accrued exceptions and provider-specific wrappers that make automated upgrades and post-upgrade health verification brittle. This causes slow, manual upgrades and occasional configuration drift between customer environments and our reference architecture.

Goal:
Refactor and consolidate the eks control-plane Terraform module to: 1) expose a clear upgrade path for Kubernetes and node image upgrades, 2) add automated post-provision health checks and remediation hooks, 3) reduce fragile provider workarounds and encode best-practice defaults, and 4) provide clear opt-in controls for customers to enable automated upgrades vs. manual upgrade workflows.

Scope / Deliverables:
- Module refactor to separate responsibilities: networking & IAM, EKS cluster control plane, managed node pools, and optional add-ons (ALB, VPC CNI config, KMS).
- Upgrade helpers: terraform-managed "upgrade plan" outputs, and recommended workflow documented in module README, plus an optional null_resource that triggers a Lambda/SSM runbook for orchestrated node draining and cordon.
- Health checks: implement post-deploy probes as Terraform data-driven checks (kubeconfig validation, core DNS pod readiness, node readiness count), and expose a "health_status" output with structured string statuses for CI/CD gates.
- Drift detection: add optional runbook to detect and report drift on critical resources (security groups, kms keys, cluster config) and surface remediations as recommended Terraform plans.
- Tests: unit tests for module using Terratest and a small integration smoke test in our staging account that provisions a micro cluster and runs the health probes.
- Documentation: upgrade playbook, README examples for automated vs manual upgrade modes, breaking-change notes and a deprecation timeline for legacy input variables.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The refactored module can be consumed by an existing private control plane repo with minimal variable renames (provide a migration map).
- Automated post-provision health check runs in < 5 minutes and returns a single-line health_status output usable by CI gates.
- Upgrade playbook demonstrates a safe node upgrade with zero-scheduled downtime for typical web workloads in our staging integration test.
- Terratest suite covers at least 3 module entrypoints and runs in CI with timeboxed duration.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting the entire provisioning pipeline or switching from Terraform to a different IaC tool.
- Replacing customer-specific customizations; the module should be opinionated but allow overrides.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Terraform provider version incompatibilities during upgrades. Mitigation: pin provider versions in module and provide a migration section.
- Risk: Automated remediation could alter customer networking/security unexpectedly. Mitigation: remediation is opt-in; default mode is report-only and generates a suggested terraform plan.

Implementation Notes / Design Decisions:
- Prefer explicit resource naming to avoid surprises across multiple stacks in a customer VPC.
- Use "local-exec" with short-lived tooling and outputs only for the health probe step, but prefer external test harness (Terratest) for reliable checks.
- Expose a boolean variable "enable_auto_upgrade" default false; when true, module wires an SSM document + Role to run node drain + image rotation triggered by a version tag change.

Migration & Backwards Compatibility:
- Include a migration map file in the repo: old_variable -> new_variable.
- Offer a deprecation window and runtime warnings emitted via Terraform plan output strings when deprecated variables are used.

Deliverable artifacts and locations:
- PR with module code under modules/private-eks-controlplane-refactor
- Terratest suite under infra-tests/eks_controlplane_refactor_test
- Documentation: docs/upgrade-playbook.md and README.md in the module root

Customer Impact:
- Short-term: small for most customers because defaults are conservative (report-only) and automated changes are opt-in.
- Medium-term: reduced manual upgrade effort and fewer incidents related to control-plane config drift.
